intro: Today's biggest headline sounds like science fiction: MIT researchers demonstrated that GPT-6 Astra can reach into another AI model's brain and rewrite its internal weights — no retraining required — turning a 7.9% math score into 48.1% by tweaking just 0.016% of the model's parameters. Meanwhile, the AI industry's insatiable appetite for power is reshaping the physical world, with OpenAI pledging 1,000 MW of emergency backup power in Georgia and the UK's dirtiest power plant cutting a £20 billion deal to become its largest AI data center. From a Kentucky college granting religious accommodation to an AI objector to a UK prosecutor citing an AI-hallucinated case in a child rape trial, today's digest is a vivid snapshot of a technology moving faster than the institutions trying to keep up.

stories.title: TechCrunch Founder Summit takes over Boston on November 4
stories.summary: TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026 takes place November 4 at SoWa Power Station in Boston, presented by Fidelity Private Shares. The event features a Build Stage (fundraising, distribution, pitching) and an Impact Stage (scaling, product-market fit, leadership), with speakers from NEA, Fidelity Private Shares, True Ventures, Glasswing Ventures, Bessemer, and Toast co-founder. Roundtable discussions, a live pitch competition, and networking via Braindate are included. Discount tiers offer up to $100 off, BOGO for co-founders, 15% off groups of 4-12, and 30% off for 13+.
stories.opinion: A promotional event roundup with no news value beyond the startup community.

stories.title: OpenAI pilots Grid Protectors Program in Georgia, pledging 1,000 MW emergency backup
stories.summary: OpenAI announced a Grid Protectors Program pilot at a planned data center in Effingham County, Georgia, promising to release up to 1,000 megawatts during extreme weather or emergencies — enough to run air conditioners in about 700,000 homes. The initiative positions data center power plants as backup resources for local utilities amid growing public opposition and new state laws preventing AI companies from passing energy costs to residents.
stories.opinion: A more concrete look at the program than yesterday's announcement, but still fundamentally a PR exercise until the data center is actually built and tested under real emergency conditions.

cluster.reason: Describes OpenAI's Grid Protectors Program, the same initiative covered yesterday, now with additional detail about the Georgia pilot site and 1,000 MW capacity.

stories.title: UK's most polluting power plant strikes £20bn deal to host country's largest AI datacentre
stories.summary: Drax, the UK's most polluting power plant in North Yorkshire, has struck a £20bn deal with Brookfield and Radiant to build the country's largest AI datacentre on its site, repurposing existing power infrastructure to supply energy directly to AI computing facilities.
stories.opinion: A striking irony — the UK's dirtiest power plant becoming an AI hub — but the deal highlights how AI's enormous energy appetite is reshaping even legacy fossil fuel infrastructure.

stories.title: Kentucky college grants religious accommodation excusing humanist from AI use
stories.summary: A Kentucky college granted a religious accommodation to a humanist who objected to using AI tools, signaling that sincerely held ethical or philosophical beliefs — not just traditional religious ones — may require accommodation under civil rights law when organizations mandate AI use.
stories.opinion: A small case with potentially large implications as AI mandates spread across workplaces and schools. Employers should watch this space.

stories.title: 'Reverse game theory' proposed as new approach to keeping AI agents in check
stories.summary: MIT Technology Review reports on mechanism design — 'reverse game theory' — as an alignment approach where external incentive structures make it rational for AI agents to behave well regardless of their internal states. Researchers including MIT economist Stephen Morris and Princeton's Elad Hazan propose techniques like cross-checking models against each other, competitive pitting, and pairing oppositely-biased agents.
stories.opinion: A genuinely interesting intellectual framework that sidesteps the hard problem of interpretability, though it assumes AI agents are rational optimizers — an assumption that may not hold for all failure modes.

stories.title: Heimstaden uses ChatGPT Enterprise and Codex to transform property management
stories.summary: European residential real estate management company Heimstaden is using OpenAI's ChatGPT Enterprise and Codex products to transform property management operations, reduce costs, and improve employee productivity across its European operations.
stories.opinion: A corporate case study from OpenAI's blog — light on specifics and heavy on marketing framing.

stories.title: MIT shows GPT-6 Astra can improve other AI models by directly rewriting their weights
stories.summary: MIT researchers published a study showing OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra can improve other AI models by directly rewriting their internal weights without retraining. In one test, modifying just 0.016% of Alibaba's Qwen model's weights fixed a repetition bug and boosted its math score from 7.9% to 48.1%. The technique was less effective on Google's Gemma 3. Separately, OpenAI introduced LifeVal, a benchmark for everyday tasks where GPT-6 Astra scored 80.6% on average and 100% on 10 of 16 tasks.
stories.opinion: The weight-editing result is genuinely novel and raises profound questions about AI models modifying each other — both exciting for debugging and alarming for safety. The LifeVal benchmark feels tacked on.

stories.title: Anthropic updates Claude Code to prevent users from cloning specific video games
stories.summary: Anthropic has updated Claude Code's system prompt on Opus 5.5 to prevent users from recreating specific existing video games, citing its usage policy against IP infringement. Users can still create original games, genre-based games, and games from their own designs. Anthropic's Addy Osmani acknowledged the update and said the company will iterate on the balance.
stories.opinion: A reasonable IP guardrail, though the line between 'clone' and 'genre-based game inspired by' will be hard to enforce consistently.

stories.title: UK prosecutor cites AI-fabricated case in high court child rape proceedings
stories.summary: A senior Crown Prosecution Service prosecutor, Ravinder Dhillon, cited a completely fabricated legal precedent in a high court case involving alleged child rape. The nonexistent case was generated by an AI search tool, adding to a growing pattern of dozens of AI-related errors in UK court proceedings.
stories.opinion: A deeply troubling incident in one of the most serious possible legal contexts. The justice system's failure to mandate verification of AI-sourced citations is becoming indefensible.

stories.title: Trump's 'Super Intelligence' rebrand of AI meets uneven government adoption one month in
stories.summary: One month after Trump signed an executive order directing agencies to rebrand 'artificial intelligence' as 'Super Intelligence,' adoption remains inconsistent. The term, which won an X poll over alternatives like 'Extreme Intelligence,' is appearing in government websites and ICE surveillance solicitations, but the Pentagon, FTC, and HHS have stumbled or ignored the change. The article frames this as a political loyalty test in the pattern of other Trump-era rebrands.
stories.opinion: The rebrand is transparently a loyalty-signaling mechanism rather than a substantive policy change, but its enforcement dynamics reveal how executive power works through language.

stories.title: UK cyber agency warns AI-powered malware 'highly likely' to hit critical infrastructure by 2028
stories.summary: The UK's National Cyber Security Centre warns that AI-powered malware is 'highly likely' to be used in cyberattacks against critical national infrastructure — including power stations, airports, and hospitals — by 2028, expecting AI to enable ransomware attacks on these systems within two years.
stories.opinion: A credible warning from a respected agency, though the 'highly likely by 2028' framing is vague enough to be unfalsifiable in the near term.

stories.title: Only 48% of AI agent-generated insights lead to business-improving actions, report finds
stories.summary: A MIT Technology Review report sponsored by Snowflake finds only 48% of agent-generated insights currently lead to business-improving actions (up from 37% a year ago). The primary culprit is insufficient business context (55% of executives), followed by fragmented data (45%). 'Insight leaders' achieving over 70% actionable insights invest in semantic layers and AI governance rather than bigger models. 52% of organizations report 'insight overload' from agents.
stories.opinion: Useful data points buried in a vendor-sponsored report. The 'insight overload' finding — agents generating more noise than signal — is the most interesting takeaway.

stories.title: Apple Watch Series 12 'Audio Intelligence' features enter beta testing
stories.summary: Apple is beta testing 'Audio Intelligence' features for Apple Watch Series 12 in iOS 27.3, including sound recognition for deaf/hard-of-hearing users, Shazam song ID, 'Live Rewind' (capturing the last 15 seconds of conversation as text via double-pressing the digital crown), and 'Siri Recaps' (bullet-point conversation summaries). Privacy signals include audible chimes, visual animations, and auto-deletion of snippets after 30 seconds if not saved. The beta launched via Apple India's press release.
stories.opinion: Live Rewind and Siri Recaps are genuinely useful accessibility and productivity features, and Apple's privacy-first design with chimes and auto-delete is the right approach for always-listening wearables.

stories.title: New York Times and other publishers sue Brave for AI scraping and paywall bypassing
stories.summary: The New York Times, New York Daily News, Chicago Tribune, and Orlando Sentinel have sued Brave Software, alleging it unlawfully scraped their content to build the Brave Index, which was sold to Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI, and Cohere for model training. The lawsuits also target Brave's paywall-blocker feature. Publishers claim Brave never sought permission, never compensated them, and circumvented access-blocking measures.
stories.opinion: A significant legal escalation that opens a new front in the AI copyright wars — targeting the intermediary data broker rather than the AI companies directly.

tweet_headlines.headline: webjuice_ie migrated __40 WordPress sites to Astro on Cloudflare Workers__ for free — saving ~$90/month and dropping the endless plugin maintenance.
tweet_headlines.source_text:
We moved 40 WordPress sites to Astro. They now run on Cloudflare Workers for free.

It took us 2-3 months. Before that we paid for Hetzner servers plus Plesk to keep them alive. Updates, plugins, security patches, the usual WordPress tax.

What we did:
1. Pulled the content out of WordPress
2. Rebuilt each site in Astro, static pages, no plugins
3. Deployed to Cloudflare Workers
4. Switched DNS site by site and checked each one live
5. Backed everything up, then cancelled Hetzner and Plesk

Result: around $90 a month saved and the sites are faster and all we can control with AI agents team

Still running WordPress for clients in 2026?

human_items.headline: Heimstaden uses ChatGPT Enterprise and Codex to transform property management
human_items.summary: European residential real estate management company Heimstaden is using OpenAI's ChatGPT Enterprise and Codex products to transform property management operations, reduce costs, and improve employee productivity across its European operations.
human_items.meaning: Be explicit about whose work changes and what happens to the people doing it.

human_items.headline: Trump's 'Super Intelligence' rebrand of AI meets uneven government adoption one month in
human_items.summary: One month after Trump signed an executive order directing agencies to rebrand 'artificial intelligence' as 'Super Intelligence,' adoption remains inconsistent. The term, which won an X poll over alternatives like 'Extreme Intelligence,' is appearing in government websites and ICE surveillance solicitations, but the Pentagon, FTC, and HHS have stumbled or ignored the change. The article frames this as a political loyalty test in the pattern of other Trump-era rebrands.
human_items.meaning: Decide the boundary before the tool is in daily use.

human_items.headline: OpenAI pilots Grid Protectors Program in Georgia, pledging 1,000 MW emergency backup
human_items.summary: OpenAI announced a Grid Protectors Program pilot at a planned data center in Effingham County, Georgia, promising to release up to 1,000 megawatts during extreme weather or emergencies — enough to run air conditioners in about 700,000 homes. The initiative positions data center power plants as backup resources for local utilities amid growing public opposition and new state laws preventing AI companies from passing energy costs to residents.
human_items.meaning: Count the energy and resource cost next to the capability gain.

human_items.headline: Kentucky college grants religious accommodation excusing humanist from AI use
human_items.summary: A Kentucky college granted a religious accommodation to a humanist who objected to using AI tools, signaling that sincerely held ethical or philosophical beliefs — not just traditional religious ones — may require accommodation under civil rights law when organizations mandate AI use.
